title: fix(sim,app): flag a STEP model imported coarser than promised; tighten its gouge verdicts, refuse past that
body:
Base is `main`. #839, which this was stacked on, has merged; `origin/main` (575f02d8) is merged into this branch.

## What changed

A STEP model whose kept mesh is coarser than the importer's 0.005 mm promise used to import with only a line on stderr. Its facets stand inside the true surface on a convex wall, so a real gouge up to the mesh's error could pass. Following the maintainer's decision on #864:

1. **Flagged.** The import records the error of the mesh it kept (held work on this branch: `step_refine`, `step::parse_with_chord`; a refinement pass that is thrown away no longer lends its tolerance to the coarser mesh that is kept). Above the cap, the model carries `schema::ReducedFidelity { chord_mm }`. It is set by `ImportModel`, `UpdateModel`, `ImportFixture` and `AddFixtureModel`, kept by a repair, restored by undo and by undoing a delete, and saved as `coarse_mm` on that entity only.
2. **Tightened while honest.** `VerifyContext::model_excess` (achieved error less the cap) is a separate field, not mixed into `gouge_tol`. The gouge laws subtract it from their tolerance while a positive tolerance is left.
3. **Refused past that.** Once the excess uses a whole tolerance, the laws read untightened and the program gate refuses each operation judged against that model, by name. The program sim does not judge either, so no gouge line is read off such a mesh.

With no flag (every model that fits the budget, STL, OBJ, every older project) `model_excess` is 0 and every law, golden and saved byte is as before.

### Laws that read the excess

| Law | Where |
|---|---|
| (b) section / tangency floor | `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:103` |
| (b2) solid law `allow` | `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:267` |
| (f) finish envelope, gouge half | `crates/sim/src/verify/finish.rs:104` |
| containment kinds' solid law (`contain_into`) | `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3203` |
| lathe axial hole verdict (`drilling::axial_warnings`) | `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:2944` |
| program sim verdict (`deviate`) | `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` (`simulate_document`), `crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs:268` (`judge`), through `model_fidelity::verdict_tol` |

The one test both the laws and the gate read is `verify::excess_floor` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`).

### Laws that do not (said, not hidden)

- **Refused on any reduced-fidelity model** (`operation::fidelity_law::excess_aware`), because their gouge laws are not threaded yet: 2D chamfer, deburr, trace, engrave, probe, the cross drill, every multi-axis and rotary kind, turning, plasma.
- **Collision laws, not tightened:** shank and holder reach (c, c3), rapids in stock (d), the turning rapid, bar-feed and holder scans. While an operation still posts the excess is under 0.01 mm.
- **Display only, unchanged:** the machined-surface classes and the viewport deviation preview still colour at 0.01 mm.
- **Fixtures** that came through the same importer: judged by their bounding box grown by the error on every side, and their mesh is not offered to the mesh law, which only ever acquits. Stock: a stock copied from a model reads that model's excess.

All of the above is filed as #904.

### A metre-unit STEP file

Since #839 it stops at the kernel's least tolerance, 0.01 mm, above the cap. It now gets the same flag and the same treatment: 0.005 mm of tolerance is left, so its mill verdicts are tightened and it still posts; the kinds listed above are refused. Scaling to millimetres before meshing was not attempted (it means transforming the kernel's shell before tessellation); it is in #904. An inch file meets the promise and is not flagged (pinned).

## What the user sees

- Model page: `Reduced fidelity: surfaces are approximated to within 0.012 mm`, with a hint: "This model was too large to import at full detail. Gouge checks against it are stricter to make up for that; when it is too coarse to check at all, its operations are refused at the post. Re-import with a larger budget to clear this."
- Import status line: `imported part - Reduced fidelity: surfaces are approximated to within 0.012 mm`.
- Post refusal: `OP: model 'part' was imported too coarsely to verify; re-import with a larger budget (surfaces are approximated to within 0.030 mm)`.
- For a kind that cannot be judged yet: `OP: model 'part' was imported at reduced fidelity (surfaces are approximated to within 0.012 mm) and this kind of operation cannot be verified against it; re-import with a larger budget`.
- The stock sim line: `stock sim did not judge this program: model 'part' was imported too coarsely to verify; re-import with a larger budget (...)`.

"Re-import with a larger budget" is the maintainer's wording; the facet budget is not a user setting yet (#904).

## MCP

- `import_model` adds `reduced_fidelity: { approximation_mm, promised_mm, note }` for such a model, and nothing for a normal one.
- `get_job` carries the same object on that model's entry only.
- Both tool descriptions say so. The `camcraft-mcp` skill text is a process file and was not edited.

## Pins

- `crates/sim/tests/model_excess.rs`: a cut 0.006 mm into a convex wall (less than the 0.0122 mm mesh error) passes at full fidelity and is convicted with the excess; a nominal ring is clean both ways; an exactly finished flat face is never a gouge at any excess; past the tolerance the law reads exactly as at full fidelity; `excess_floor` only tightens.
- `crates/app/tests/model_fidelity.rs`: an over-budget import is flagged with its own error and one that fits is not (through undo, redo, update, repair-style update, delete and undo, stock copy); the inch fixture is not flagged and the metre sample is, at 0.01 mm with 0.005 mm left; a project keeps the flag, and one without it saves back byte for byte; the program verdict convicts a floor cut 0.006 mm deep on the reduced model and passes it at full fidelity, while an exact flat face posts on both; a model at 0.03 mm is refused by name, with no gouge line even for a path sunk 1 mm, and does not post; a 2D chamfer is refused on any reduced model; a coarse fixture's box grows and its mesh is withheld; MCP `import_model` and `get_job` facts.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/model_fidelity.rs`: the model page shows the flag and the achieved error for a reduced model and nothing for a normal one (AccessKit labels).
- Held from the earlier worker: `step_refine::tests::*`, `crates/app/tests/step_fidelity.rs`.

## Gate

On the final head `215da948` (`e7d4f807` + three merges of `origin/main`, the last at 2437098f, + one test commit):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green, 4 steps, 0 failed, 20.9 min. sim suites (18 binaries), motion suites (16), app suites (210), ui suites (12, the lib with `model_fidelity` included).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests`: green, 53 test binaries, 431 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Merges of `main` (it moved twice while the gate ran):

- `crates/app/src/commands/update_model.rs`: both sides added fields and a builder to `UpdateModel` (#826's plate snapshot and `keeping_plate`; this PR's `coarse_mm` / `prev_coarse_mm`, `with_fidelity`, `keeping_fidelity`). Both kept; `apply` and `invert` write both.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, the two `contain_into` calls: #843 passes its shared `cutter` where the tool was, this PR adds the model's excess as the last argument. Both kept. #843's two new test contexts (`tool_body_bands`, `tool_body_judged`) take `..Default::default()`.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs` merged clean: `main`'s union arc reading and the `model_excess` floor are both there, and the reading still uses the plain `gouge_tol`. New pin for the two together: `verify_arc_reading::boundary_mode_judges_the_union_joints_against_the_tightened_floor` (a sharp vertex on an old arc joint is convicted between the plain and the tightened floor, clean outside it). #839's `boundary_mode_keeps_the_old_joints_so_a_sharp_vertex_on_one_stays_convicted` still passes.
- The third merge was clean.

The diff touches 42 existing test files with one line each (`..Default::default()` on their `VerifyContext` literal); no golden, snapshot or expected value changed.

## Not exercised

- The envelope law (f) and the containment solid law are tightened through the same helper as (b), but have no fixture-level pin on a reduced-fidelity model (#904).
- No real over-budget model (30 M facets) was imported; the pins force the small fixture over a test-only budget.
- The GUI was not launched; the page is pinned structurally only. Snapshot PNGs are untouched.
- The release tier and the heavy `--ignored` lanes were not run.

Changelog: A STEP model imported coarser than 0.005 mm is flagged as reduced fidelity (model page, MCP, project file); gouge checks against it are tightened by the excess, and its operations are refused at the post once it is too coarse to verify
Effort: max (escalated once, from high)

Fixes #864
